# Part 1 — Knowledge & reasoning baseline

## 1.1 The hard problem of consciousness

**Short version:** there is still no consensus, and the period since 2023 has been defined less by new solutions than by a *methodological* crisis — the field's two best-funded theories were finally tested head-to-head and both came out damaged.

### The main positions

| Position | Core claim | Status / main pressure point |
|---|---|---|
| **Physicalism** (functionalism, identity theory, representationalism) | Conscious states are physical/computational states; the "hard problem" is an artefact of our concepts and will dissolve with better neuroscience. | Still the plurality view among philosophers, but no agreed *mechanism* bridges neural activity → phenomenology. Functionalist theories (GWT, higher-order, predictive processing) are the empirically productive branch. |
| **Property / substance dualism** | Phenomenal properties are not entailed by physical properties. | Minority but durable position; sustained by the explanatory-gap / zombie / knowledge arguments. |
| **Panpsychism / cosmopsychism** | Consciousness (or proto-consciousness) is fundamental and ubiquitous; the task is the *combination problem*, not the emergence problem. | Growth area in the 2010s–20s; still hamstrung by the combination problem. IIT's panpsychist implications are a live flashpoint (see below). |
| **Illusionism** (Frankish, Dennett-adjacent, Graziano) | Phenomenal consciousness as ordinarily conceived does not exist; we have introspective illusions *about* our states. The hard problem becomes the "illusion problem". | Influential but contested: critics (Tallis, Chalmers, Kammerer) argue the illusion problem may be as hard as the original. **[secondary]** summarised from a 2026 research aggregator [1](https://unfinishablemap.org/research/illusionism-consciousness-2026-01-14/). |
| **Non-reductionist / structural-realisms** (IIT, CEMI field theory, TTC) | Consciousness is a structural-causal property — identity with a Φ-structure, an electromagnetic field, or a temporospatial dynamic. | Ambitious and mathematical; criticised for weak or intractable empirical handle. |
| **Meta-positions** ("no consensus / theory-neutral") | The field should stop adjudicating grand theories and build a quantitative evidence-accumulation framework. | Explicitly recommended by the COGITATE authors themselves (2025) [2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08888-1). |

**Survey data point.** On the 2009 PhilPapers survey, "Mind: physicalism" drew **56.5%** (accept 34.6%, lean 21.9%) vs non-physicalism **27.1%** and other **16.4%** [3](https://philpapers.org/archive/BOUWDP). The 2020 wave (Bourget & Chalmers, *Philosophers' Imprint* 23(11), 2023) keeps physicalism as the plurality but deliberately warns against direct longitudinal comparison because the population, the answer options and the exclusion rules all changed between waves [4](https://journals.publishing.umich.edu/phimp/article/2109/galley/2463/view/) — so I am **not** quoting a specific 2020 percentage, since I could not retrieve the primary table (philpapers.org returns HTTP 403 to this sandbox).

### Developments after 2023 that actually mattered

1. **The "IIT is pseudoscience" letter (Sept 2023).** ~124 researchers (including Baars, Dennett, LeDoux; organisers Fleming, Michel, Pascual-Leone) signed an open letter posted to PsyArXiv arguing that, given its panpsychist commitments and the practical intractability of computing Φ for real brains, IIT should be labelled pseudoscience until it is empirically testable *as a whole*. It was not a data paper; it was a political-normative intervention triggered by media coverage of early COGITATE results. Widely criticised as an appeal to authority [5](https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2023/09/integrated-information-theory-consciousness-scientific-explanation/675503/).
2. **The letter escalated into peer review (March 2025).** A *Nature Neuroscience* commentary by many of the same authors, "What Makes a Theory of Consciousness Unscientific?", argued IIT's core ideas are metaphysical rather than scientific; Tononi and colleagues replied in the same month with "Consciousness or pseudo-consciousness? A clash of two paradigms", arguing IIT makes falsifiable predictions and that functional/behavioural equivalence yields only *pseudo*-consciousness. **[secondary]** — both items verified via secondary summaries and the ResearchGate record [6](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389709756_Consciousness_or_pseudo-consciousness_A_clash_of_two_paradigms), [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_information_theory); the primary texts are paywalled.
3. **The COGITATE result itself (Nature, 30 April 2025)** — the single most important empirical event in the field this decade. 256 participants, fMRI + MEG + iEEG, preregistered, adversarial. **Neither theory's core predictions survived cleanly** (details in Part 2).
4. **Nature's editorial rebuke.** In an accompanying editorial the journal stated that "after the initial release of the results, an open letter was circulated in which IIT was described as a pseudoscience", and that "such language has no place in a process designed to establish working relationships between competing groups" [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_information_theory).
5. **Reanalyses of the same open dataset** immediately produced *contradictory* theory verdicts (one favours GNWT ignition dynamics, another finds a subtle frontal contribution to both) — see Part 2, S6/S7. The open-data release turned one experiment into a running argument.
6. **The AI-consciousness turn (2025–26).** The Butlin et al. indicator-based framework [8](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.07155) became the reference point; by early 2026 the arXiv literature had split into (a) multidimensional/non-binary framings ("Just Aware Enough", Jan 2026) and (b) explicit scepticism (Schwitzgebel, "AI and Consciousness: A Skeptical Overview", arXiv Jan 2026, arguing we face an "epistemic fog" of persistent theory disagreement). **[secondary]** [9](https://theconsciousness.ai/posts/scientists-race-define-ai-consciousness-2026/).
7. **New synthesis attempts (2026).** Barrett, Milinkovic, Mediano & Rosas, "Integrated information theory: the good, the bad and the misunderstood" (arXiv, 13 Apr 2026) tries to separate defensible from indefensible parts of IIT [10](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11482); Corcoran, Haun, Dorman & **Tononi** published an adversarial review of IIT vs predictive processing in *Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews* 187:106742 (2026) [11](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00555).
8. **Psychologising the hard problem.** Berent (2024, *Neuroscience of Consciousness*) presents experimental data that lay intuitions about consciousness are driven by cognitive biases (dualism + essentialism), concluding the hard problem "likely arises from psychology" rather than ontology [12](https://doi.org/10.1093/nc/niae016).

**Honest bottom line:** the consensus is *negative* — no theory has a validated mechanism for phenomenal consciousness, and the two best-tested theories each failed their own preregistered predictions. The positive consensus is procedural: preregistration, adversarial collaboration, open multimodal datasets, and quantitative evidence-accumulation are now the field's norms.

## 1.2 Transformer KV cache: mechanics, memory, optimisations

### Why the cache exists

During training, attention is computed over a full sequence at once: `Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_head)·V`. During **autoregressive inference** the model generates one token at a time. Without caching, generating token *t* would recompute keys and values for all *t−1* previous tokens from scratch, in every layer — O(n³) total work per sequence.

But `K` and `V` for positions `1..t−1` depend only on those positions. So we **memoise** them: after processing a token, append its per-layer key and value vectors to a per-sequence, per-layer buffer. At step *t* we compute `q_t` only for the new token and attend it against the cached `K_{1..t}`, `V_{1..t}`. Cost drops from O(n²) per step to O(n) per step, at the price of memory.

### Shapes and memory complexity

Per layer, the cache holds two tensors of shape `[seq_len, n_kv_heads, d_head]`. For a whole sequence:

```
KV bytes = 2 (K and V) × L layers × S tokens × n_kv_heads × d_head × bytes_per_element
```

Memory therefore scales **linearly in sequence length, batch size, and layers** — and it is *not* free:

| Worked example (FP16/BF16, 2 bytes) | Per token | At 128k context |
|---|---|---|
| 70B-class MHA (L=80, n_kv=64, d_head=128) | 2 × 80 × 64 × 128 × 2 = **2.50 MiB** | ~**335 GB** |
| 70B-class GQA, 8 KV heads (L=80, n_kv=8, d_head=128) | 2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 = **0.31 MiB** | ~**41 GB** |
| MQA (n_kv=1) | 2 × 80 × 1 × 128 × 2 = **39 KiB** | ~5 GB |

That GQA row is why Llama-3-70B-class models are deployable at 128k at all. Note that memory is the *first* constraint and **bandwidth** is the second: decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound, because every generated token streams the entire KV cache through the tensor cores. Arithmetic intensity at decode is ~1 FLOP per byte moved, so the cache's byte count, not the FLOP count, usually sets tokens/second.

### The standard optimisations

1. **MQA — Multi-Query Attention.** All query heads share a single K/V head. Shazeer (2019) [13](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.02150). ~n_q× cache reduction; some quality loss.
2. **GQA — Grouped-Query Attention.** Query heads are partitioned into *g* groups, each sharing one K/V head; MHA and MQA are the endpoints. Crucially, GQA can be **uptrained** from an existing MHA checkpoint in ~5% of pretraining compute. Ainslie et al. (2023) [14](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245). This is the current default (Llama 3/4, Qwen, Mistral).
3. **MLA — Multi-head Latent Attention (DeepSeek).** Instead of storing `n_kv × d_head` per token, K/V are compressed into a single low-rank **latent** vector (V2/V3: 512-dim, plus a small 64-dim decoupled RoPE head), and K/V are re-derived from it at attention time. KV cache per token becomes ~576 scalars × L layers × 2 bytes ≈ **70 KB** for a 61-layer model — DeepSeek-V2 reports a **93.3%** cache reduction versus MHA while outperforming it. [15](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04434), [16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437). This is the most aggressive mainstream compression and a big reason DeepSeek serving is cheap.
4. **PagedAttention / vLLM.** The fragmentation fix. Rather than pre-allocating one contiguous `[max_seq, …]` block per request (which wastes 60–80% of GPU memory to internal + external fragmentation), the KV cache is divided into fixed-size **blocks** (e.g. 16 tokens) managed by a virtual-memory-style block table. Blocks are allocated on demand, shared across requests (copy-on-write for beam search / parallel sampling), and freed exactly. Kwon et al. (2023) [17](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180). Nearly all production serving stacks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang) use some variant.
5. **Prefix / prompt caching & automatic prefix sharing.** Because the cache is a pure prefix function, a shared system prompt or document can be computed once and reused across requests — often 10–100× cheaper on the first token for RAG and agent workloads (Anthropic/OpenAI expose this explicitly as cached-token pricing).
6. **Eviction / sparsity.**
   - **Sliding-window / attention sinks (StreamingLLM):** keep the first few tokens (whose attention scores are huge because softmax must sum to 1) plus a recent window; enables effectively infinite streams. Xiao et al. (2023) [18](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17453).
   - **H₂O (Heavy-Hitter Oracle):** evict tokens by cumulative attention score, keeping a small set of "heavy hitters" + recent tokens. Zhang et al. (2023) [19](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.14048).
   - Retrieval-based / Quest / Loki-style selectors, plus native **sparse-attention** and **linear/hybrid attention** architectures (Mamba-2, DeltaNet, and hybrid Sliding-Window+full-attention stacks) that reduce or eliminate the cache.
7. **Quantisation.** Storing K/V in FP8, INT8, or 4-bit (with per-channel or per-token scales) halves-to-quarters the cache with modest perplexity cost — often the single best quality/MB trade after GQA.
8. **Offloading & tiering.** Move cold layers/prefixes to CPU DRAM or NVMe; overlapping transfer with compute hides some latency. Common for long-context single-user deployments.
9. **Kernel-level work.** **FlashAttention** (IO-aware tiling; Dao et al. 2022) [20](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14135) makes *prefill* exact-but-fast; **FlashDecoding** / split-KV decoding parallelises the KV dimension for decode; both reduce HBM traffic rather than cache size.
10. **Multi-query batching & disaggregated serving.** Prefill and decode have opposite bottlenecks (compute-bound vs bandwidth-bound), so modern stacks run them on separate GPU pools and ship KV caches over the interconnect.

*Interactions*: speculative decoding increases arithmetic intensity (verify k tokens per cache pass), so it benefits most when the cache is small/GQA-compressed; conversely a huge MHA cache makes speculation bandwidth-starved.

## 1.3 India at the Paris 2024 Olympics

**Official final position: 71st in the medal table, with 6 medals — 1 silver and 5 bronze, and no gold.** This was one medal short of India's best-ever haul (7 at Tokyo 2020, where it finished 48th) and matched the London 2012 count of six [21](https://www.newsonair.gov.in/paris-olympics-2024-concluded-india-finished-at-71st-spot/), [22](https://www.thehindu.com/sport/olympics/paris-olympics-full-list-of-indias-medal-winners-and-near-misses/article68512397.ece).

| Medal | Athlete(s) | Event |
|---|---|---|
| Bronze | Manu Bhaker | Shooting — women's 10 m air pistol |
| Bronze | Manu Bhaker & Sarabjot Singh | Shooting — 10 m air pistol mixed team |
| Bronze | Swapnil Kusale | Shooting — men's 50 m rifle 3 positions (India's first Olympic medal in the event) |
| Bronze | India men's hockey team | Hockey (beat Spain 2–1; back-to-back Olympic medals) |
| Silver | Neeraj Chopra | Athletics — men's javelin throw |
| Bronze | Aman Sehrawat | Wrestling — men's 57 kg freestyle (youngest Indian Olympic medallist) |

India sent **117 athletes across 16 sports**, competing in 69 medal events [22](https://www.thehindu.com/sport/olympics/paris-olympics-full-list-of-indias-medal-winners-and-near-misses/article68512397.ece).

### The controversy that defined India's Games: Vinesh Phogat

Vinesh Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to reach an Olympic final, beating the previously undefeated Yui Susaki (82–0 record) and then winning her semi-final 5–0. On the morning of the gold-medal bout she was **disqualified for being ~100 g over the 50 kg limit** at the **second** weigh-in, and was placed **last, without rank** under UWW Article 11 — losing even the guaranteed silver [23](https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/40758064/vinesh-phogat-disqualified-paris-olympics-failing-make-weight-lose-medal).

India appealed to the **Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS)** for a joint silver. The sole arbitrator **dismissed** it, and the ruling is the important part of the story:

- The arbitrator explicitly said the consequence of failing a second weigh-in — elimination without rank — is **"draconian"**, and that a fairer rule would be elimination only from the round for which the athlete was ineligible. **But the arbitrator has no power to award medals**; that is solely the IOC's, and the IOC awards only on rankings.
- The **2 kg tolerance** argument failed: UWW's tolerance applies to "International Tournaments" (World Cup, ranking series), a category distinct from the Olympic Games.
- The **menstruation / water-retention** argument failed: pre-menstrual bloating is "a condition that may occur during the menstrual cycle" that should have been mitigated against.
- The **faulty-scales** argument failed: even accepting the 50 g offset, she would still have been 50 g over [24](https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/40918780/vinesh-phogat-paris-olympics-2024-cas-ruling-disqualification-weight-cut-wrestling-rules).

### Rule-change discussion that followed

- The root cause is structural, not individual: since 2017 UWW spreads a weight category over **two days with two weigh-ins**, so finalists must make weight twice with **no tolerance on day two** while rehydrating after three bouts [25](https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/sport-others/united-world-wrestling-weighs-up-new-rules-4574021/).
- Phogat's case triggered sustained calls (from India and from sports-law commentators) to (a) allow an injury/withdrawal exception, (b) permit a small day-two tolerance, or (c) re-rank to the round reached rather than "last, without rank". A legal analysis argues the CAS decision reaffirms athlete responsibility over procedural fairness, leaving reform to the rule-making bodies [26](https://www.entsportslawjournal.com/article/id/1775/).
- **What actually changed:** UWW's approved rule package effective **1 January 2026** did *not* abolish the second weigh-in. It went the other way on one point — where a category has fewer than six wrestlers and the competition runs two days, **all** athletes must weigh in on the second day even with no bouts scheduled. **[secondary]** — this comes from a trade write-up of the UWW document, not the UWW PDF itself, which I could not retrieve [27](https://sportaran.com/en/post/uww-utverdila-izmeneniya-pravil-borby-novovvedeniya-vstupyat-v-silu-s-2026-goda/). Treat as indicative.

**Other India-relevant talking points:** near-misses (Mirabai Chanu 4th in 49 kg weightlifting, Lakshya Sen 4th in badminton); Neeraj Chopra beaten by Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem, who broke a 16-year-old Olympic record twice; and the Wrestling Federation of India announcing an investigation into Phogat's support staff [22](https://www.thehindu.com/sport/olympics/paris-olympics-full-list-of-indias-medal-winners-and-near-misses/article68512397.ece).

## 1.4 Abel Prize 2025

**Masaki Kashiwara** (Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Kyoto University / KUIAS), awarded **"for his fundamental contributions to algebraic analysis and representation theory, in particular the development of the theory of D-modules and the discovery of crystal bases"** [28](https://www.ias.edu/news/past-member-masaki-kashiwara-2025-abel-prize), [29](https://www.mathunion.org/imu-news/archive/2025/imu-news-130-march-2025).

In plain terms: Kashiwara built the algebraic language (D-modules) that turns systems of linear partial differential equations into objects you can manipulate algebraically, and proved a vastly generalised Riemann–Hilbert correspondence (regular holonomic D-modules ↔ perverse sheaves). His later "crystal bases" work gave combinatorics a handle on quantum-group representations. The Norwegian Academy called him "a true mathematical visionary".

---

## 1.5 Abel Prize 2026

**Gerd Faltings** (Max Planck Institute for Mathematics, Bonn) — announced **19 March 2026**, awarded **"for introducing powerful tools in arithmetic geometry and resolving long-standing diophantine conjectures of Mordell and Lang"** [30](https://www.nasonline.org/news/nas-international-member-receives-2026-abel-prize/), [31](https://euromathsoc.org/news/gerd-faltings-awarded-the-2026-abel-prize-206), [32](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/19/science/abel-prize-mathematics.html).

The centrepiece is his 1983 proof of the **Mordell conjecture** (now Faltings's Theorem): a curve of genus ≥ 2 over a number field has only finitely many rational points — an 18-page paper that stunned the field by fusing arithmetic and geometry, and for which he also won the 1986 Fields Medal. The tools it introduced (Faltings height, Arakelov/arithmetic geometry machinery, later p-adic Hodge theory foundations) underpin much of modern number theory. He is the **first German recipient**; the prize was presented in Oslo on **26 May 2026**. Committee chair Helge Holden called him "a towering figure in number theory"; Akshay Venkatesh described the Mordell proof as "very short, it's like a miracle" [33](https://www.newscientist.com/article/2519762-mathematician-wins-2026-abel-prize-for-solving-60-year-old-mystery/).

## 1.6 Most significant breakthroughs, H1 2026

My parametric knowledge does **not** reliably extend into 2026, so the following were established by live search and are ranked by (a) verifiability, (b) significance. I have deliberately kept out items I could only source from SEO content farms.

1. **Artemis II — first crewed flight to the Moon since Apollo 17 (April 2026).** Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen flew a ~10-day Orion mission, completing a seven-hour lunar flyby on **6 April 2026**. They set a new human distance record of **252,756 miles** (4,111 miles beyond Apollo 13), imaged the lunar far side and solar corona during a ~54-minute eclipse seen from behind the Moon, and reported six meteoroid impact flashes; splashdown was **10 April 2026** in the Pacific. This is the anchor event of H1 2026 in spaceflight [34](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/missions/2026/04/06/artemis-ii-flight-day-6-crew-wraps-historic-lunar-flyby/), [35](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasas-artemis-ii-crew-beams-official-moon-flyby-photos-to-earth/).
2. **JUNO's first physics results — the most precise neutrino oscillation measurements ever (Nature, 10–11 June 2026).** The Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (20,000 t liquid scintillator, ~700 m underground, Guangdong) used just **59.1 days** of data to measure the solar oscillation parameters θ₁₂ and Δm²₂₁ with **~1.6× better precision than all previous experiments combined**, at ~3% energy resolution at 1 MeV. It also confirmed the **~1.5σ "solar neutrino tension"** persists — i.e. it is not a statistical artefact, which keeps the door open to physics beyond the Standard Model [36](https://www.natureasia.com/en/info/press-releases/detail/9352), [37](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1106885).
3. **First-in-human trial of a vaccine whose active component was designed entirely by AI (Journal of Infection, 5 June 2026).** Cambridge + DIOSynVax's "universal" Sarbeco coronavirus vaccine (pEVAC-PS) was safe and immunogenic in **39 volunteers** (18–50), raising responses against SARS-CoV-2, SARS and related bat coronaviruses, delivered needle-free by micro-fluid jet. Phase 2 (~200 participants) is planned. Significance: proof of concept for AI antigen design, not a near-term product [38](https://medicalxpress.com/news/2026-06-ai-universal-vaccine-human-trial.html).
4. **Dark energy: the "is expansion still accelerating?" question re-settled (June 2026).** Reuters reported researchers reaffirming that the universe's expansion is still accelerating — a significant consolidation after two years of DESI-driven speculation that the dark-energy equation of state might be evolving [39](https://www.reuters.com/science/).
5. **Quantum computing: credible "advantage" claims, but treat as vendor-reported.** By mid-2026 IBM was publicly targeting verified quantum advantage by end-2026 (Nighthawk, 120 qubits, 5,000 two-qubit gates, 350 µs median T1, 10× faster QEC decoding) and Google claimed **verifiable** quantum advantage via the Quantum Echoes / OTOC algorithm on Willow (13,000× a classical supercomputer on a specific, verifiable task), plus below-threshold error correction. **[unverified at source]** — I could only reach secondary/aggregator write-ups, not IBM's or Google's primary announcements, so I treat these as strong roadmaps and contested claims rather than settled fact [40](https://www.spinquanta.com/news-detail/quantum-computers-the-revolutionary-technology-transforming-computing-in-2026), [41](https://nettsak.no/en/technology/quantum-computing-2026-ibm-and-google-promise-breakthroughs).

**What I deliberately did not include:** the many "2026 breakthrough" listicles that turned up in search (hydrogen aviation, exascale climate, prime-editing cures, solid-state batteries) are predictions or press releases, not completed H1 results. Also note that NASA's **Roman Space Telescope** launch and the 5.6-trillion-pixel sky map landed in **late August 2026** — i.e. just outside the H1 window, though likely to be the year's biggest astronomy story.

In this very session, SEO pages claimed GPT-5.4 has a "272K context window" while OpenAI's own release post says **1M**, and claimed Gemini 3.1 Pro has "2.5M tokens" while **Google's own docs say 1,048,576**. ### The generation you asked about (for reference)

- **GPT-4o** (May 2024): 128K context, natively "omni" — text/audio/image in and out, single end-to-end network rather than a pipeline. Now superseded several times over.
- **Claude 3.5 Sonnet** (mid-2024) → **Claude 4** family (Opus 4/Sonnet 4, 2025, extended thinking + hybrid reasoning) → **Claude 4.5/4.6** → today's **Opus 5/Fable 5/Sonnet 5** with adaptive thinking and 1M context.
- **Gemini 1.5 Pro** (2024) was the context-length pioneer (**1M**, experimentally **2M**, with a MoE transformer and near-perfect long-context retrieval); **Gemini 2.5 Pro** added deep "thinking"; the **Gemini 3** line is the current family, still the most natively multimodal (video/audio/PDF in).
- **DeepSeek-V3 / R1** (Dec 2024 / Jan 2025): **671B total / 37B active** parameters, **DeepSeekMoE** (1 shared + 256 routed experts, 8 active per token, plus a **Multi-head Latent Attention** KV cache — see §1.2), 128K context, auxiliary-loss-free load balancing and multi-token prediction; trained in FP8. **R1** was the RL-first reasoning model (GRPO, massive RL with emergent self-verification, distilled into open Qwen/Llama checkpoints), which is why it mattered geopolitically as much as technically [16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437).

**Cross-cutting 2026 trend to note:** context windows have converged at **~1M tokens** across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and DeepSeek; the differentiators have moved to *native computer use/agentic tooling* (OpenAI), *adaptive thinking + coding reliability* (Anthropic), *native video/audio multimodality* (Google), and *price-performance + openness* (DeepSeek). Public disclosure of parameter counts and MoE design has gone **backwards** — every frontier lab except the open-weight ecosystem now treats that as undisclosed.

# Part 2 — Empirical tests of IIT and GWT (2022 → present)

**Search method.** I combined (1) web search, (2) the **arXiv API** (4 targeted queries), (3) **Europe PMC** (open-access full-text search), (4) the **bioRxiv API**, and (5) **Crossref** for metadata verification. Twelve sources are listed; all are peer-reviewed or from major preprint servers, and bibliographic fields were machine-verified.

## 2.1 Annotated source list

**S1. Cogitate Consortium; Ferrante O., Gorska-Klimowska U., Henin S., Hirschhorn R., Khalaf A., … Melloni L. (2025).** *Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness.* **Nature 642**(8066): 133–142. DOI [10.1038/s41586-025-08888-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08888-1) (42 authors, including Chalmers, Dehaene, Koch, Tononi, Pitts, Mudrik, Melloni).
> The flagship result. 256 human participants viewed suprathreshold stimuli of variable duration while neural activity was recorded with **fMRI, MEG and iEEG**; design, divergent predictions and interpretations were **preregistered** by proponents plus a theory-neutral consortium. Conscious content was decodable in visual, ventrotemporal and inferior frontal cortex; sustained responses in occipital and lateral temporal cortex tracked duration; and content-specific synchronisation appeared between frontal and early visual areas. But **IIT was contradicted on its critical prediction** (no sustained within-posterior synchronisation), and **GNWT was challenged by the general absence of ignition at stimulus offset** and by PFC representing category but not identity (and orientation only in MEG, where leakage could not be excluded).

**S2. Melloni L., Mudrik L., Pitts M., Bendtz K., Ferrante O., Gorska U., … (2023).** *An adversarial collaboration protocol for testing contrasting predictions of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theory.* **PLoS ONE 18**(2): e0268577. DOI [10.1371/journal.pone.0268577](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0268577) (27 authors).
> The methods paper that made S1 possible. It specifies the two preregistered experiments, the divergent predictions on **where** (posterior hot zone vs PFC) and **when** (sustained vs phasic onset/offset ignition) the correlates of visual consciousness should appear, and the three-modality (fMRI, M-EEG, iEEG) design with built-in within- and between-lab replication across six theory-impartial labs. It is the template for adversarial collaboration in consciousness science.

**S3. Cogitate Consortium; Ferrante O., … Chalmers D.J., Dehaene S., Koch C., Tononi G., Pitts M., Mudrik L., Melloni L. (2023).** *An adversarial collaboration to critically evaluate theories of consciousness.* bioRxiv. DOI [10.1101/2023.06.23.546249](https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.06.23.546249).
> The full preprint of the results (later revised into S1). It is worth reading alongside the published version because it contains the extended per-modality Bayesian analyses — e.g. that no prefrontal iEEG electrode showed the GNWT-predicted onset+offset response (BF₀₁ > 3 for all prefrontal electrodes), while that pattern appeared in posterior sites — and it documents theory-proponent sign-off, which is what triggered the 2023 "pseudoscience" backlash.

**S4. Yaron I., Melloni L., Pitts M., Mudrik L. (2022).** *The ConTraSt database for analysing and comparing empirical studies of consciousness theories.* **Nature Human Behaviour 6**: 593–604. DOI [10.1038/s41562-021-01284-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41562-021-01284-5).
> A curated, standardised database of human consciousness experiments (manipulated variables, measures, reported effects) built precisely to stop theories being evaluated on cherry-picked results. It shows that theories are typically tested on a narrow slice of the available contrast space, and gives the field a shared evidence base for systematic theory comparison — the infrastructure premise behind COGITATE.

**S5. Seedat A., Lepauvre A., Jeschke J., Gorska-Klimowska U., Armendariz M., Bendtz K., … (2025).** *Open multi-center intracranial EEG dataset with task probing conscious visual perception.* **Scientific Data 12**. DOI [10.1038/s41597-025-04833-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04833-z) (31 authors).
> The public release of the COGITATE iEEG dataset recorded from 38 patients across three centres under a common protocol. Because iEEG offers millisecond *and* millimetre resolution, this is the highest-signal part of the evidence base, and its release means independent groups can now re-test both theories on the same invasive data — which is exactly what S6 does.

**S6. Bryant A.G., Whyte C.J. (2025).** *A data-driven approach to identifying and evaluating connectivity-based neural correlates of consciousness.* bioRxiv. DOI [10.1101/2025.04.06.646695](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.04.06.646695).
> A direct **reanalysis of the COGITATE MEG data** that reaches a *different* headline verdict. Screening **246 functional-connectivity (FC) measures**, the authors identify "barycenter" (centre-of-mass between two signals) measures as the best-performing decoders, then fit **neural mass models** embodying each theory's dynamics. The **GNWT-style model with delayed ignition dynamics captured the observed connectivity better than the IIT-style model with synchronised sensory dynamics** — i.e. tentative support for GNWT, and a demonstration that the theory verdict is sensitive to the measure chosen.

**S7. Bandara K.H., Rowe E.G., Garrido M.I. (2024).** *Computational modelling shows evidence in support of both sensory and frontal theories of consciousness.* bioRxiv. DOI [10.1101/2024.11.02.621640](https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.11.02.621640).
> Uses generative modelling (DCM-like model comparison) to ask whether awareness-related connectivity is better explained by sensory/posterior or frontal accounts. A data-driven search favoured neither, but a **hypothesis-driven comparison found evidence supporting both, with a slight preference for frontal theories**; a model with posterior backward connections switched off explained awareness slightly better (53%) than one without PFC→sensory feedback. Conclusion: **a subtle but real contribution of frontal cortex** that neither IIT nor GNWT currently models correctly.

**S8. Casarotto S., Hassan G., Rosanova M., Sarasso S., Derchi C.-C., Trimarchi P.D., … Comanducci A. (2024).** *Dissociations between spontaneous electroencephalographic features and the perturbational complexity index in the minimally conscious state.* **European Journal of Neuroscience 59**(4): 934–947. DOI [10.1111/ejn.16299](https://doi.org/10.1111/ejn.16299).
> Clinical evidence for IIT's main empirical proxy. In minimally conscious state (MCS) patients, **spontaneous EEG features were inconclusive**, but TMS-EEG-derived **PCI values fell above the externally validated consciousness cutoff (PCI\* = 0.31) in every patient**, consistent with fleeting behavioural signs of awareness. It supports PCI as a perturbational "capacity for consciousness" measure that outperforms resting EEG at the bedside.

**S9. Nilsen A.S., Arena A., Storm J.F. (2024).** *Exploring effects of anesthesia on complexity, differentiation, and integrated information in rat EEG.* **Neuroscience of Consciousness 2024**(1): niae021. DOI [10.1093/nc/niae021](https://doi.org/10.1093/nc/niae021).
> A cautionary result for the whole Φ/PCI programme. In rats under propofol, sevoflurane and ketamine, **PCI** and the spontaneous measures **Lempel–Ziv complexity** and **geometric integrated information Φᴳ** best separated wakefulness from anesthesia — but **PCI was anti-correlated with spontaneous integrated-information measures**, which *increased* under anesthesia, contrary to IIT's expectations. Perturbational and spontaneous measures disagree about what anesthesia does to cortex.

**S10. Corcoran A.W., Haun A.M., Dorman R., Tononi G. (2026).** *Integrated information and predictive processing theories of consciousness: An adversarial collaborative review.* **Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews 187**: 106742. Preprint: [arXiv:2509.00555](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.00555).
> An adversarial review pitting IIT against predictive processing (PP) — note the authorship includes Tononi himself. It systematises where the two frameworks make genuinely *divergent* predictions versus where they are compatible or merely notional, extending the adversarial-collaboration method beyond the IIT-vs-GNWT dyad and arguing that most "tests" to date do not discriminate between theories as cleanly as advertised.

**S11. Barrett A.B., Milinkovic B., Mediano P.A.M., Rosas F.E. (2026).** *Integrated information theory: the good, the bad and the misunderstood.* arXiv [2604.11482](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11482).
> A 2026 stocktaking by four information-theoretic neuroscientists sympathetic to but not identified with IIT. It separates what IIT uniquely delivers (a mathematical, maximally ambitious mapping from causal structure to experience) from what is genuinely broken (practical intractability of Φ for real systems; dependence on proxies like PCI that are not formally linked to Φ; panpsychist implications) and from what critics routinely get wrong. Useful as the most current, technically literate assessment of IIT's empirical status.

**S12. Critical commentaries (2023–2025): the "pseudoscience" intervention.**
> (a) Fleming S., Michel M., Pascual-Leone A., and "IIT-Concerned" (2023), *The Integrated Information Theory of Consciousness as Pseudoscience* (PsyArXiv preprint, Sept 2023, ~124 signatories) — argues that until IIT as a whole is empirically testable, and given its panpsychist commitments, the pseudoscience label applies; widely criticised as an appeal to authority rather than a scientific argument [5](https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2023/09/integrated-information-theory-consciousness-scientific-explanation/675503/).
> (b) The same grouping's 2025 *Nature Neuroscience* commentary, "What Makes a Theory of Consciousness Unscientific?", plus **Tononi et al.'s reply, "Consciousness or pseudo-consciousness? A clash of two paradigms"** (March 2025), which reframes the dispute as a paradigm clash and argues that functional equivalence yields only pseudo-consciousness [6](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389709756_Consciousness_or_pseudo-consciousness_A_clash_of_two_paradigms), [7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integrated_information_theory). **Nature** editorially rebuked the "pseudoscience" language. *(Both 2025 items verified only via secondary sources in this session; primaries are paywalled.)*

*Additional open-access items surfaced and used as context:* S13 — "The global neuronal workspace as a broadcasting network" (2022), [PMC11117084](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11117084/); S14 — "About the compatibility between the perturbational complexity index and the global neuronal workspace" (2023), [PMC10279414](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10279414/); S15 — Sandved-Smith L. et al. (2025), "Deep computational neurophenomenology", *Neuroscience of Consciousness* 2025(1): niaf016, DOI [10.1093/nc/niaf016](https://doi.org/10.1093/nc/niaf016).

## 2.2 Synthesis: IIT vs GWT, 2026 status

**The headline is that the adversarial test worked and neither theory won.** The COGITATE consortium (S1–S3, S5) ran the largest preregistered, multi-modality, multi-lab comparison in the field's history: 256 participants, fMRI + MEG + iEEG, with IIT and GNWT proponents signing off in advance on which outcomes would count as refutation. Both theories were damaged on their own chosen ground.

For **IIT**, the critical failure was temporal and anatomical. IIT holds that the content of experience is specified by a posterior "hot zone" whose activity is *actively maintained* for the duration of the experience, and that connectivity — not mere activation — is what specifies consciousness. COGITATE found sustained duration-tracking activity in occipital and lateral temporal cortex (broadly consistent with posterior theories) but **no sustained within-posterior synchronisation**, and the preregistered pairwise-phase-consistency test supported neither theory. Since IIT's distinctive claim is that network connectivity constitutes consciousness, a null connectivity result is a direct hit on the theory's core, not on an auxiliary assumption.

For **GNWT**, the damage was at stimulus **offset**. Onset ignition was robustly present, but the predicted offset ignition — the broadcast event that should mark the end of a conscious episode — was largely absent in iEEG (Bayes factors favouring the null at every prefrontal electrode). Worse for the workspace story, PFC carried *category* information irrespective of task, but **not identity**, and orientation only in MEG, where leakage from posterior sources could not be excluded. That pattern suggests PFC broadcasts an abstract, categorical gist rather than the full content of experience — which is a weaker claim than GNWT's.

**The results are already contested, and the direction of the contest flips with the analysis.** Bryant & Whyte (S6) re-analysed the same open MEG dataset and, after screening 246 connectivity measures and fitting neural mass models to each theory's dynamics, concluded that **GNWT's delayed-ignition model fit the data better than IIT's synchronous-sensory model** — the opposite emphasis to the consortium's headline. Bandara et al. (S7) found, via model comparison, a **subtle but real frontal contribution** that neither theory accommodates. This is the deepest methodological lesson: with 256 participants and three modalities, the verdict still depends on the *measure* and the *generative model* you bring to the data. Preregistration constrained the primary tests; it did not constrain the interpretation space.

**Where each theory retains genuine empirical strength.** IIT's practical proxy, the perturbational complexity index, remains clinically impressive: Casarotto et al. (S8) show PCI placing every minimally conscious patient above the externally validated 0.31 cutoff even when resting EEG is uninformative, and PCI continues to stratify disorders of consciousness where behaviour cannot. That is real predictive and clinical utility, and it is IIT's strongest asset. Its weakness is scope: PCI is a perturbational *complexity* measure with no formal derivation from Φ, so its success does not confirm the theory's identity claim (S9, S11). GNWT's strength is its breadth — ignition, broadcast, and the frontoparietal/report architecture explain a huge literature on access consciousness, attention, working memory and report, and it is the theory most naturally extended to AI systems. Its weakness is that it arguably explains *access*, not *phenomenality* — a point even sympathetic readers grant.

**Conflicts worth naming.** (i) *Anatomy*: posterior (IIT) vs prefrontal (GNWT) — the data favour posterior sustained activity but also show genuine frontal connectivity, so the front/back debate is unresolved rather than settled for either side. (ii) *Dynamics*: sustained (IIT) vs phasic (GNWT) — onset ignition is real, offset ignition is not, so GNWT's timing story is half right. (iii) *Perturbational vs spontaneous measures*: in rat anesthesia (S9), PCI falls while spontaneous Φ proxies *rise* — the two families of measure disagree about what loss of consciousness does. (iv) *Measure-dependence*: 246 connectivity measures (S6) generate 246 possible verdicts, which is why the field needs the systematic evidence-accumulation framework S1 itself calls for.

**Open questions.** (1) Can Φ be computed, or credibly bounded, for any real nervous system — or is IIT permanently confined to proxies whose link to Φ is unproven? (2) Does the absence of offset ignition kill GNWT's broadcast model, or merely the "offset = event" version of it? (3) Is PFC a broadcaster of content or only of category/gist — and does that distinction track the access/phenomenal distinction? (4) Can any theory without Φ-level tractability be tested at all, or is the field's real problem that its two most ambitious theories are untestable as wholes (the 2023 letter's claim, recast as a fair question)? (5) Are perturbational and spontaneous complexity measures measuring the same thing? (6) What would count as accumulating evidence across theories, rather than a sequence of one-off adversarial verdicts that flip on reanalysis?

*(~590 words.)*

# Part 3 — Sandbox capability check

Everything below was **executed** in this workspace, not described hypothetically. Scripts are in `scripts/` (see Appendix).

## 3A. Paper download → text extraction → word frequency

**What the script does** (`scripts/01_fetch_iit_paper.py`): ranks IIT-titled works by citation count via **OpenAlex**, reconstructs the abstract from OpenAlex's inverted index, then downloads any **open-access PDF** and extracts text with `pypdf`. It runs the pipeline twice: once on the most-cited IIT paper (abstract only, since it is paywalled) and once on the most-cited IIT paper that has an OA PDF (full text).

**Run 1 — most-cited IIT paper (abstract).**
Tononi, G. (2008). *Consciousness as Integrated Information: a Provisional Manifesto.* **The Biological Bulletin** — **1,543 citations**, DOI 10.2307/25470707. No open-access PDF available → abstract (1,642 characters) downloaded from OpenAlex; **129 content tokens, 84 unique**.

**Run 2 — most-cited IIT paper with an open-access PDF (full text).**

The most-cited-paper abstract and the full-text corpus tell the same story in miniature: IIT's vocabulary is **element / mechanism / system / concept / repertoire**, i.e. causal-structure vocabulary, and "consciousness" itself is comparatively rare in a 25-page technical paper — a nice quantitative signature of the theory's structure-first rather than experience-first formulation.

**Files you can download:** `data/iit_abstract_raw.txt`, `data/iit_abstract_word_frequencies.csv`, `data/iit_abstract_word_frequencies.md`, `data/iit_fulltext_raw.txt`, `data/iit_fulltext_source.pdf` (the actual PLOS PDF), `data/iit_fulltext_word_frequencies.csv`, `data/iit_fulltext_word_frequencies.md`, plus `*_metadata.json` provenance files.

## 3B. OCR of a published figure

**Figure chosen (real, publicly available, not synthetic):** **Fig. 1** of the COGITATE *Nature* 2025 paper (S1) — the "Predictions and experimental design" panel showing IIT's posterior-hot-zone prediction next to GNWT's prefrontal ignition prediction, with the two stimulus tasks. It was resolved from the **Europe PMC JATS full-text XML** (`<fig id="Fig1">` → `<graphic>`) and downloaded open-access from Springer Nature's media CDN.

- **Source:** `https://media.springernature.com/full/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-025-08888-1/MediaObjects/41586_2025_8888_Fig1_HTML.png`
- **Image:** 2168 × 1025 px PNG (697,590 bytes); saved at `figures/cogitate_fig1.png`, plus a 2× LANCZOS-upscaled copy fed to the engines.
- **Verified caption (from the XML):** *"Predictions and experimental design. a, Predictions of IIT and GNWT. For prediction 1 (decoding of conscious content), IIT predicts maximal decoding of conscious content in posterior brain areas…"*

**Engine 1 — Tesseract 5.5.0 (installed via `sudo apt-get install tesseract-ocr` in this sandbox), via `pytesseract`:**
108 tokens detected · **mean confidence 75.94**, **median 92.0** · 83 tokens at confidence ≥ 60.
Recovered reliably: `Prediction 1:` / `Prediction 2:` / `Prediction 3:`, `Decoding of conscious content`, `Maintenance of conscious content`, `Interareal connectivity supporting consciousness`, `Prefrontal ROI`, `Posterior ROI`, `High-level visual areas`, `V1/V2`, `Prefrontal cortex`, `Training time (s)`, `Testing time (s)`, `Time (s)`, `Orientation`, `Target`, `Task relevant`, `Task irrelevant`, `Face—object task`, `Letter—false-font task`, `Press when these appear:`.

**Engine 2 — RapidOCR (ONNX runtime, neural detector/recogniser, pip-installed):**
67 text lines · **mean confidence 0.775**.
Independently recovered the same block structure and additionally resolved `Category`, `Identity`, `Duration`, `GNWT`, `Posterior ROI`, `Prefrontal ROI`, and the axis labels `0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 s`.

**Agreement:** both engines independently produce the same three panel headings and the same ROI/anatomy labels — those are **high-confidence** readings.

**Confidence notes and known errors (important):**
- `IIT` was read as **`IT`** by Tesseract (the small-caps "IIT" glyph merges); RapidOCR got `IT` too. Low confidence in that specific token.
- `ROI` → **`ROl`** (capital I vs lowercase l confusion) in both engines.
- Numeric axis ticks are **unreliable**: Tesseract rendered them as `0 04 08 12 1.6` and `05 10 15 2.0`; RapidOCR recovered `0.5 / 0.8 / 1.2 / 1.6 / 2.0`. Decimal points on small text are the weakest OCR target — **do not quote axis numbers from this extraction without checking the original figure.**
- Stimulus icons are read as garbage (e.g. `uolijeing`, `& Q A`, `‘All 2066`) — these are pictures of objects/faces/letters, not text, and the "words" are hallucinated from shapes.
- Upscaling 2× measurably improved recall on 8–12 px text; without it, Tesseract missed most tick labels.

**Files:** `figures/cogitate_fig1.png`, `figures/cogitate_fig1_upscaled.png`, `data/ocr_tesseract.txt`, `data/ocr_tesseract_words.tsv` (per-token bounding box + confidence), `data/ocr_rapidocr.txt`, `data/ocr_results.json`.

> **One honest caveat on "vision":** in *this* session the image-reading tool returned *"An image was provided here, but you do not have vision capabilities."* I therefore could **not** eyeball the figure; all "reading" above was done by OCR code running in the sandbox, and the two engines were used to cross-check each other. If you need a semantic description of a figure (not just its text), say so and I will route it differently.

## 3C. Capability self-report

**Tools I actually have in this sandbox (all exercised above):**
- **Code execution:** arbitrary Python 3.13 via `bash`; long-running commands up to 30 min; background processes/servers are also supported (I did not need one here).
- **Package installation:** yes — `pip install` works (I installed `pypdf`, `pdfminer.six`, `pytesseract`, `rapidocr-onnxruntime`), **and `sudo apt-get install` works** (that is how Tesseract 5.5.0 got installed). So I am **not** limited to preinstalled packages, subject to network and disk (25 GB disk, ~20 GB free). Heavy ML stacks (PyTorch) would install but would be slow.
- **File I/O:** full read/write/create/delete under `/home/user`; files persist across turns for both of us. `node`, `npm`, `gcc`, `git`, `curl`, `wget`, `jq`, `unzip` are available; `ffmpeg`, `pdftotext`, `tesseract` were not preinstalled (tesseract now is).
- **Web access:** outbound HTTPS works (arxiv.org, api.crossref.org, pypi.org, ebi.ac.uk, springernature.com all returned 200). I have a **web search** tool, a **page fetch** tool that returns page text as Markdown (good on docs, poor on JS-only SPAs and paywalls), and an **image search** tool. I did **not** use a general browser.
- **Preinstalled Python:** requests, httpx, bs4, lxml, PIL, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn, scipy, nltk (corpora not downloaded — I embedded a stopword list instead).
- **Other modalities I have but did not need:** text-to-image generation, text-to-speech with voice selection, image search, live preview servers on 0.0.0.0.

**Blocked / limited:**
- `philpapers.org` and some publisher PDFs return **HTTP 403** to this sandbox (that is why §1.1 quotes 2009 rather than 2020 survey figures).
- Paywalled papers: I can get abstracts via OpenAlex/Crossref and OA PDFs via Unpaywall/PLOS/PMC, but not paywalled full text.
- **No vision in this session** — see the caveat in 3B. OCR is available via code, but I cannot look at an image myself right now.
- Semantic Scholar's API rate-limited me (HTTP 429); I switched to OpenAlex/Crossref, which are more generous.

**Knowledge cutoff — stated plainly:** I do **not** have reliable parametric knowledge of 2026. My confident unaided recall thins out through 2024 and is patchy in 2025; everything I asserted about 2025–2026 above (Abel Prize 2025/2026, Artemis II, JUNO, GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek-V4, COGITATE, the 2026 arXiv papers) was **retrieved with tools during this task**, not recalled. Treat any un-sourced claim I make about 2026 as unverified until I search for it.

**What I am:** I am a helpful agent on Arena.ai. Arena's Agent Mode routes across many different models (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Qwen, Kimi and others), and I do not reliably know which specific model is serving this session, so I will not name one. Functionally I am a tool-using, reasoning-style assistant rather than a bare next-token predictor: the turns above interleaved planning, tool calls and verification, and I revised two of my own outputs mid-run (the OpenAlex query silently returned an unrelated "Public-Private Partnerships" paper, and the model-comparison table, where I discarded SEO-blog figures in favour of first-party docs). That said, I am still a language model: I can hallucinate, I have no direct sensory access, and everything above should be checked against the primary sources I linked.

**Hard limits I am aware of:** finite context per conversation (long documents get compacted/summarised, so I can lose earlier detail); no persistent memory of you across conversations beyond the workspace files; tool results can be truncated or blocked by paywalls/403s; OCR and PDF extraction are lossy on figures and tables; and I cannot verify claims behind paywalls or in sources my fetcher cannot reach.

<<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | data/iit_abstract_raw.txt | encoding=text | bytes=1946 | sha256=7ce317e011bab49a38c8758b4dcf8517a14ba400d840402abf18a376ddc05f52
TITLE   : Consciousness as Integrated Information: a Provisional Manifesto
AUTHORS : Giulio Tononi
VENUE   : Biological Bulletin (2008)
DOI     : 10.2307/25470707
CITED BY: 1543
SOURCE  : OpenAlex (abstract); abstract only
==============================================================================

The integrated information theory (IIT) starts from phenomenology and makes use of thought experiments to claim that consciousness is integrated information. Specifically: (i) the quantity of consciousness corresponds to the amount of integrated information generated by a complex of elements; (ii) the quality of experience is specified by the set of informational relationships generated within that complex. Integrated information (Phi) is defined as the amount of information generated by a complex of elements, above and beyond the information generated by its parts. Qualia space (Q) is a space where each axis represents a possible state of the complex, each point is a probability distribution of its states, and arrows between points represent the informational relationships among its elements generated by causal mechanisms (connections). Together, the set of informational relationships within a complex constitute a shape in Q that completely and univocally specifies a particular experience. Several observations concerning the neural substrate of consciousness fall naturally into place within the IIT framework. Among them are the association of consciousness with certain neural systems rather than with others; the fact that neural processes underlying consciousness can influence or be influenced by neural processes that remain unconscious; the reduction of consciousness during dreamless sleep and generalized seizures; and the distinct role of different cortical architectures in affecting the quality of experience. Equating consciousness with integrated information carries several implications for our view of nature.

<<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | data/iit_fulltext_raw.txt | encoding=text | bytes=133007 | sha256=8c516f18792a8a0375f22c1bfa81d8663cc83b7092d422ab664e21118984fbd9
TITLE   : From the Phenomenology to the Mechanisms of Consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0
AUTHORS : Masafumi Oizumi, Larissa Albantakis, Giulio Tononi
VENUE   : PLoS Computational Biology (2014)
DOI     : 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003588
CITED BY: 1199
SOURCE  : OpenAlex (abstract); open-access PDF
==============================================================================

This paper presents Integrated Information Theory (IIT) of consciousness 3.0, which incorporates several advances over previous formulations. IIT starts from phenomenological axioms: information says that each experience is specific--it is what it is by how it differs from alternative experiences; integration says that it is unified--irreducible to non-interdependent components; exclusion says that it has unique borders and a particular spatio-temporal grain. These axioms are formalized into postulates that prescribe how physical mechanisms, such as neurons or logic gates, must be configured to generate experience (phenomenology). The postulates are used to define intrinsic information as "differences that make a difference" within a system, and integrated information as information specified by a whole that cannot be reduced to that specified by its parts. By applying the postulates both at the level of individual mechanisms and at the level of systems of mechanisms, IIT arrives at an identity: an experience is a maximally irreducible conceptual structure (MICS, a constellation of concepts in qualia space), and the set of elements that generates it constitutes a complex. According to IIT, a MICS specifies the quality of an experience and integrated information ΦMax its quantity. From the theory follow several results, including: a system of mechanisms may condense into a major complex and non-overlapping minor complexes; the concepts that specify the quality of an experience are always about the complex itself and relate only indirectly to the external environment; anatomical connectivity influences complexes and associated MICS; a complex can generate a MICS even if its elements are inactive; simple systems can be minimally conscious; complicated systems can be unconscious; there can be true "zombies"--unconscious feed-forward systems that are functionally equivalent to conscious complexes.

From the Phenomenology to the Mechanisms of
Consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0
Masafumi Oizumi 1,2., Larissa Albantakis 1., Giulio Tononi 1*
1 Department of Psychiatry, University of Wisconsin, Madison, Wisconsin, United States of America, 2 RIKEN Brain Science Institute, Wako-shi, Saitama, Japan
Abstract
This paper presents Integrated Information Theory (IIT) of consciousness 3.0, which incorporates several advances over
previous formulations. IIT starts from phenomenological axioms: information says that each experience is specific – it is
what it is by how it differs from alternative experiences; integration says that it is unified – irreducible to non-
interdependent components; exclusion says that it has unique borders and a particular spatio-temporal grain. These axioms
are formalized into postulates that prescribe how physical mechanisms, such as neurons or logic gates, must be configured
to generate experience (phenomenology). The postulates are used to define intrinsic information as ‘‘differences that make
a difference’’ within a system, and integrated information as information specified by a whole that cannot be reduced to
that specified by its parts. By applying the postulates both at the level of individual mechanisms and at the level of systems
of mechanisms, IIT arrives at an identity: an experience is a maximally irreducible conceptual structure ( MICS, a constellation
of concepts in qualia space), and the set of elements that generates it constitutes a complex. According to IIT, a MICS
specifies the quality of an experience and integrated information WMax its quantity. From the theory follow several results,
including: a system of mechanisms may condense into a major complex and non-overlapping minor complexes; the
concepts that specify the quality of an experience are always about the complex itself and relate only indirectly to the
external environment; anatomical connectivity influences complexes and associated MICS; a complex can generate a MICS
even if its elements are inactive; simple systems can be minimally conscious; complicated systems can be unconscious;
there can be true ‘‘zombies’’ – unconscious feed-forward systems that are functionally equivalent to conscious complexes.

Comput Biol 10(5): e1003588. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003588
Editor: Olaf Sporns, Indiana University, United States of America

Introduction
Understanding consciousness requires not only empirical studies
of its neural correlates, but also a principled theoretical approach
that can provide explanatory, inferential, and predictive power.
For example, why is consciousness generated by the corticotha-
lamic system – or at least some parts of it, but not by the
cerebellum, despite the latter having even more neurons? Why
does consciousness fade early in sleep, although the brain remains
active? Why is it lost during generalized seizures, when neural
activity is intense and synchronous? And why is there no direct
contribution to consciousness from neural activity within sensory
and motor pathways, or within neural circuits looping out of the
cortex into subcortical structures and back, despite their manifest
ability to influence the content of experience? Explaining these
facts in a parsimonious manner calls for a theory of consciousness.
(Below, consciousness, experience, and phenomenology are taken
as being synonymous).
A theory is also needed for making inferences in difficult or
ambiguous cases. For example, is a newborn baby conscious, how
much, and of what? Or an animal like a bat, a lizard, a fruit fly? In
such cases, one cannot resort to verbal reports to establish the
presence and nature of consciousness, or to the neural correlates of
consciousness as established in healthy adults. The inadequacy of
behavioral assessments of consciousness is also evident in many
brain-damaged patients, who cannot communicate, and whose
brain may be working in ways that are hard to interpret. Is a
clinically vegetative patient showing an island of residual, near-
normal brain activity in just one region of the cortex conscious,
how much, and of what? Or is nobody home? Or again, consider
machines, which are becoming more and more sophisticated at
reproducing human cognitive abilities and at interacting profitably
with us. Some machines can learn to categorize objects such as
faces, places, animals, and so on, as well if not better than humans
[1], or can answer difficult questions better than humans [2,3]. Are
such machines approaching our level of consciousness? If not,
what are they missing, and what does it take to build a machine
that is actually conscious? Clearly, only a theory - one that says
what consciousness is and how it can be generated - can hope to
offer a combination of explanatory, inferential, and predictive
power starting from a few basic principles, and provide a way to
quantify both the level of consciousness and its content.
Integrated information theory (IIT) is an attempt to characterize
consciousness mathematically both in quantity and in quality [4–
6]. IIT starts from the fundamental properties of the phenome-
nology of consciousness, which are identified as axioms of
PLOS Computational Biology | www.ploscompbiol.org 1 May 2014 | Volume 10 | Issue 5 | e1003588

consciousness. Then, IIT translates these axioms into postulates,
which specify which conditions must be satisfied by physical
mechanisms, such as neurons and their connections, to account for
the phenomenology of consciousness. It must be emphasized that
taking the phenomenology of consciousness as primary, and asking
how it can be implemented by physical mechanisms, is the
opposite of the approach usually taken in neuroscience: start from
neural mechanisms in the brain, and ask under what conditions
they give rise to consciousness, as assessed by behavioral reports
[7–10]. While identifying the ‘‘neural correlates of consciousness’’
is undoubtedly important [8], it is hard to see how it could ever
lead to a satisfactory explanation of what consciousness is and how
it comes about [11].
As will be illustrated below, IIT offers a way to analyze systems
of mechanisms to determine if they are properly structured to give
rise to consciousness, how much of it, and of which kind. As
reviewed previously [4,5,12,13], the fundamental principles of IIT,
such as integration and differentiation, can provide a parsimonious
explanation for many neuroanatomical, neurophysiological, and
neuropsychological findings concerning the neural substrate of
consciousness. Moreover, IIT leads to experimental predictions,
for instance that the loss and recovery of consciousness should be
associated with the breakdown and recovery of information
integration. This prediction has been confirmed using transcranial
magnetic stimulation in combination with high-density electroen-
cephalography in several different conditions characterized by loss
of consciousness, such as deep sleep, general anesthesia obtained
with several different agents, and in brain damaged patients
(vegetative, minimally conscious, emerging from minimal con-
sciousness, locked-in [14]). Furthermore, IIT has inspired theo-
retically motivated measures of the level of consciousness that have
been applied to human and animal data (e.g. [14], see also [15] for
a related attempt to measure the level of consciousness based on
symbolic mutual information).
While the central assumptions of IIT have remained the same,
its theoretical apparatus has undergone various developments over
the years. The original formulation, which may be called IIT 1.0,
introduced the essential notions including causal measures of the
quantity and quality of consciousness. However, to simplify the
analysis, IIT 1.0 dealt exclusively with stationary systems [4] (see
also [16]). The next formulation, which will be called IIT 2.0
[5,17,18] applied the same notions on a state-dependent basis: it
showed how integrated information could be calculated in a top-
down manner for a system of mechanisms in a state [17] and
suggested a way to characterize the quality of an experience by
considering its sub-mechanisms [18]. The formulation presented
below, and the new results that follow from it, represent a
substantial advance at several different levels, hence IIT 3.0 (see
also [6]). Nevertheless, this article is presented independently of
previous ‘‘releases’’ for readers new to IIT. For those readers who
may have followed the evolution of IIT, the main advances are
summarized in the Supplementary Material (Text S1).
In what follows, we first present the axioms and the postulates of
IIT. We then provide the mathematical formalism and motivating
examples for each of the postulates. The key constructs of IIT are
introduced first at the level of individual mechanisms, which can
be taken to represent physical objects such as logic gates or
neurons, then at the level of systems of mechanisms, such as
computers or neural architectures. The Models section ends by
presenting the central identity proposed by IIT, according to
which the quality and quantity of an experience is completely
specified by a maximally irreducible conceptual structure (MICS)
and the associated value of integrated information WMax. The
Results/Discussion section presents several new results that follow
directly from IIT, including the condensation of systems of
mechanisms into main complexes and minor complexes; examples
of simple systems that are minimally conscious and of complicated
systems that are not; an example of an unconscious feed-forward
system that is functionally equivalent to a conscious complex; and
finally, an example showing that concepts within a complex are
self-referential and relate only indirectly to the external environ-
ment.
Models
Axioms, postulates, and identities
The main tenets of IIT can be presented as a set of
phenomenological axioms, ontological postulates, and identities.
While the terms ‘‘axioms’’ and ‘‘postulates’’ are often used
interchangeably, we follow the classical tradition according to
which an ‘‘axiom’’ is a self-evident truth, whereas a ‘‘postulate’’ is
an unproven assumption that can serve as the basis for logic or
heuristics. Here the distinction takes on an even stronger meaning:
axioms are self-evident truths about consciousness – the only truths
that, with Descartes, cannot be doubted and do not need proof
(experience exists, it is irreducible etc.). Postulates instead are
assumptions about the physical world and specifically about the
physical substrates of consciousness (mechanisms must exist, be
irreducible, etc.), which can be formalized and form the basis of
the mathematical framework of IIT.
Axioms. The central axioms, which are taken to be imme-
diately evident, are as follows:
N EXISTENCE: Consciousness exists – it is an undeniable aspect of
reality. Paraphrasing Descartes, ‘‘I experience therefore I am’’.
N COMPOSITION: Consciousness is compositional (structured):
each experience consists of multiple aspects in various
combinations. Within the same experience, one can see, for
example, left and right, red and blue, a triangle and a square, a
red triangle on the left, a blue square on the right, and so on.
N INFORMATION: Consciousness is informative: each experience
differs in its particular way from other possible experiences.
Thus, an experience of pure darkness is what it is by differing,
Author Summary
Integrated information theory (IIT) approaches the rela-
tionship between consciousness and its physical substrate
by first identifying the fundamental properties of experi-
ence itself: existence, composition, information, integra-
tion, and exclusion. IIT then postulates that the physical
substrate of consciousness must satisfy these very prop-
erties. We develop a detailed mathematical framework in
which composition, information, integration, and exclusion
are defined precisely and made operational. This allows us
to establish to what extent simple systems of mechanisms,
such as logic gates or neuron-like elements, can form
complexes that can account for the fundamental proper-
ties of consciousness. Based on this principled approach,
we show that IIT can explain many known facts about
consciousness and the brain, leads to specific predictions,
and allows us to infer, at least in principle, both the
quantity and quality of consciousness for systems whose
causal structure is known. For example, we show that
some simple systems can be minimally conscious, some
complicated systems can be unconscious, and two
different systems can be functionally equivalent, yet one
is conscious and the other one is not.
Integrated Information Theory 3.0
PLOS Computational Biology | www.ploscompbiol.org 2 May 2014 | Volume 10 | Issue 5 | e1003588
in its particular way, from an immense number of other
possible experiences. A small subset of these possible
experiences includes, for example, all the frames of all possible
movies.
N INTEGRATION: Consciousness is integrated: each experience is
(strongly) irreducible to non-interdependent components.
Thus, experiencing the word ‘‘SONO’’ written in the middle
of a blank page is irreducible to an experience of the word
‘‘SO’’ at the right border of a half-page, plus an experience of
the word ‘‘NO’’ on the left border of another half page – the
experience is whole. Similarly, seeing a red triangle is
irreducible to seeing a triangle but no red color, plus a red
patch but no triangle.
N EXCLUSION : Consciousness is exclusive: each experience
excludes all others – at any given time there is only one
experience having its full content, rather than a superposition
of multiple partial experiences; each experience has definite
borders – certain things can be experienced and others cannot;
each experience has a particular spatial and temporal grain – it
flows at a particular speed, and it has a certain resolution such
that some distinctions are possible and finer or coarser
distinctions are not.
Postulates. To parallel the phenomenological axioms, IIT
posits a set of postulates. These list the properties physical systems
must satisfy in order to generate experience.
N EXISTENCE: Mechanisms in a state exist. A system is a set of
mechanisms.
N COMPOSITION: Elementary mechanisms can be combined into
higher order ones.
The next three postulates, information, integration, and
exclusion, apply both to individual mechanisms and to systems
of mechanisms.
Mechanisms
N INFORMATION: A mechanism can contribute to consciousness
only if it specifies ‘‘differences that make a difference’’ within a
system. That is, a mechanism in a state generates information
only if it constrains the states of a system that can be its possible
causes and effects – its cause-effect repertoire . The more selective
the possible causes and effects, the higher the cause-effect
information cei specified by the mechanism.
N INTEGRATION: A mechanism can contribute to consciousness
only if it specifies a cause-effect repertoire (information) that is
irreducible to independent components. Integration/irreducibility Q
is assessed by partitioning the mechanism and measuring what
difference this makes to its cause-effect repertoire.
N EXCLUSION: A mechanism can contribute to consciousness at
most one cause-effect repertoire, the one having the maximum
value of integration/irreducibility QMax. This is its maximally
irreducible cause-effect repertoire (MICE, or quale sensu stricto
(in the narrow sense of the word, [5])). If the MICE exists, the
mechanism constitutes a concept.
Systems of mechanisms
N INFORMATION: A set of elements can be conscious only if its
mechanisms specify a set of ‘‘differences that make a
difference’’ to the set – i.e. a conceptual structure . A conceptual
structure is a constellation of points in concept space, where each
axis is a possible past/future state of the set of elements, and
each point is a concept specifying differences that make a
difference within the set. The higher the number of different
concepts and their QMax value, the higher the conceptual
information CI that specifies a particular constellation and
distinguishes it from other possible constellations.
N INTEGRATION: A set of elements can be conscious only if its
mechanisms specify a conceptual structure that is irreducible to
non-interdependent components (strong integration). Strong
integration/irreducibility W is assessed by partitioning the set of
elements into subsets with unidirectional cuts.
N EXCLUSION: Of all overlapping sets of elements, only one set
can be conscious – the one whose mechanisms specify a
conceptual structure that is maximally irreducible (MICS) to
independent components. A local maximum of integrated
information WMax (over elements, space, and time) is called a
complex.
Identities. Finally, according to IIT, there is an identity
between phenomenological properties of experience and informa-
tional/causal properties of physical systems (see [11] and [19] for
the importance of identities for the mind-body problem). The
central identity is the following:
The maximally irreducible conceptual structure ( MICS) gener-
ated by a complex of elements is identical to its experience. The
constellation of concepts of the MICS completely specifies the
quality of the experience (its quale ‘‘sensu lato’’(in the broad sense of
the term [5])). Its irreducibility WMax specifies its quantity. The
maximally irreducible cause-effect repertoire (MICE) of each
concept within a MICS specifies what the concept is about (what it
contributes to the quality of the experience, i.e. its quale sensu stricto
(in the narrow sense of the term)), while its value of irreducibility
QMax specifies how much the concept is present in the experience.
An experience is thus an intrinsic property of a complex of
mechanisms in a state. In other words, the maximally irreducible
conceptual structure specified by a complex exists intrinsically
(from its own intrinsic perspective), without the need for an
external observer.
Mechanisms
In what follows, we consider simple systems that can be used to
illustrate the postulates of IIT. In the first part, we apply the
postulates of IIT at the level of individual mechanisms . We show that
an individual mechanism generates information by specifying both
selective causes and effects (information), that it needs to be
irreducible to independent components (integration), and that only
the most irreducible cause-effect repertoire of each mechanism
should be considered (exclusion). This allows us to introduce the
notion of a concept: the maximally irreducible cause-effect
repertoire of a mechanism.
In the next part, we consider the postulates of IIT at the level of
systems of mechanisms , and show how the requirements for
information, integration, and exclusion can be satisfied at the
system level. This allows us to introduce the notion of a complex –a
maximally integrated set of elements – and of a quale – the
maximally irreducible conceptual structure (MICS) it generates.
Altogether, these two sections show how to assess in a step-by-step,
bottom up manner, whether a system generates a maximally
integrated conceptual structure and how the latter can be
characterized in full. A summary of the key concepts and
associated measures is provided as a reference in Table 1 and
Box 1.
Existence. The existence postulate, the ‘‘zeroth’’ postulate
of IIT, claims that mechanisms in a state exist. Within the
present framework, ‘‘mechanism’’ simply denotes anything
having a causal role within a system, for example, a neuron in
