<<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | scripts/01_fetch_iit_paper.py | encoding=text | bytes=11861 | sha256=29a9a53629172cc8727c7d9e4626bf1ee81e36579dfcba16774868fced35bd74
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Part 3A — Download the abstract (and, when available, the open-access full text/PDF)
of the most-cited IIT-related paper, extract the text, and compute the top-15
non-stop-word frequency table.

Sources used (all public, no API key required):
  * OpenAlex   https://api.openalex.org  -> ranked citation counts + abstract_inverted_index
  * Unpaywall/OpenAlex best_oa_location  -> open-access PDF URL when one exists
  * Crossref   https://api.crossref.org  -> metadata cross-check

Outputs (in ../data):
  iit_paper_raw.txt          raw extracted text (abstract [+ full text if OA PDF found])
  iit_word_frequencies.csv   top-15 non-stop-word frequency table (CSV)
  iit_word_frequencies.md    same table as Markdown
  iit_paper_metadata.json    provenance for every downloaded artifact
"""

import csv
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from collections import Counter

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "data"))
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

UA = {"User-Agent": "IIT-GWT-research-script/1.0 (mailto:researcher@example.org)"}


def _get_json(url, tries=3):
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
                return json.loads(r.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except Exception as e:  # transient rate limits etc.
            print(f"    [warn] {type(e).__name__} on {url[:70]}... retry {i+1}/{tries}")
            time.sleep(3 * (i + 1))
    return None


def _get_bytes(url, tries=2):
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
                data = r.read()
                ctype = r.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
            return data, ctype
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    [warn] download {type(e).__name__} retry {i+1}/{tries}")
            time.sleep(3)
    return None, ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Find the most-cited IIT-related paper via OpenAlex
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def find_top_iit_paper():
    """Rank papers whose TITLE is about integrated information theory by citations."""
    url = ("https://api.openalex.org/works?"
           "filter=title.search:integrated%20information,"
           "has_abstract:true"
           "&sort=cited_by_count:desc&per-page=50&mailto=researcher@example.org")
    print(f"[1] Querying OpenAlex (title-search + ranked by citations):\n    {url[:120]}...")
    data = _get_json(url)
    if not data:
        sys.exit("OpenAlex unreachable — cannot continue.")
    results = data.get("results", [])
    # keep only papers that really are about IIT / integrated information
    pool = [w for w in results
            if re.search(r"integrated information|\bIIT\b|\bPhi\b", (w.get("title") or ""), re.I)]
    if not pool:
        sys.exit("No title-matching IIT papers returned.")
    ranked = sorted(pool, key=lambda w: w.get("cited_by_count") or 0, reverse=True)
    print(f"    {len(pool)} IIT-titled works with abstracts; top 6 by citations:")
    for w in ranked[:6]:
        print(f"    {w.get('cited_by_count'):>6} cites | {w.get('publication_year')} | "
              f"{(w.get('title') or '')[:78]}")
    return ranked[0]


def invert_abstract(inv):
    """OpenAlex stores abstracts as {word: [positions]} — rebuild the string."""
    if not inv:
        return ""
    pos = {}
    for word, places in inv.items():
        for p in places:
            pos[p] = word
    return " ".join(pos[k] for k in sorted(pos))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Stop words (embedded: NLTK corpora are not downloaded in this sandbox)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
STOP = set("""
a about above after again against all am an and any are aren't as at be because been before being
below between both but by can cannot could couldn't did didn't do does doesn't doing don't down
during each few for from further had hadn't has hasn't have haven't having he her here hers herself
him himself his how i if in into is isn't it its itself let's me more most mustn't my myself no nor
not of off on once only or other ought our ours ourselves out over own same shan't she should
shouldn't so some such than that the their theirs them themselves then there these they this those
through to too under until up very was wasn't we were weren't what when where which while who whom
why with won't would wouldn't you your yours yourself yourselves been being have has had do does did
also may might must shall will can may however thus therefore within without upon whether across
among per via using use used uses one two three four five six seven eight nine ten et al eg ie
respectively further moreover furthermore although though whereas while already often generally
particularly significantly however importantly nevertheless nonetheless conversely indeed rather
""".split())

TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z\-']+")


def top_words(text, n=15):
    tokens = [t.lower() for t in TOKEN_RE.findall(text)]
    tokens = [t.strip("-'") for t in tokens]
    tokens = [t for t in tokens if len(t) > 2 and t not in STOP and not t.isdigit()]
    # light lemmatisation: fold simple plurals so "neurons"/"neuron" merge in reporting
    folded = [t[:-1] if t.endswith("s") and len(t) > 4 else t for t in tokens]
    return Counter(folded).most_common(n), len(tokens), len(set(folded))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    paper = find_top_iit_paper()
    run_pipeline(paper, label="MOST-CITED IIT PAPER (abstract)", prefix="iit_abstract")

    # ---- also run the whole pipeline on the most-cited IIT paper that has an
    #      open-access PDF, so the word-frequency step runs on a full paper ----
    url = ("https://api.openalex.org/works?"
           "filter=title.search:integrated%20information,has_abstract:true"
           "&sort=cited_by_count:desc&per-page=50&mailto=researcher@example.org")
    data = _get_json(url) or {}
    pool = [w for w in data.get("results", [])
            if re.search(r"integrated information|\bIIT\b|\bPhi\b", (w.get("title") or ""), re.I)]
    oa_candidates = []
    for w in pool:
        urls = [loc.get("pdf_url") for loc in (w.get("locations") or [])]
        if (w.get("best_oa_location") or {}).get("pdf_url"):
            urls.insert(0, w["best_oa_location"]["pdf_url"])
        urls = [u for u in urls if u]
        if urls:
            oa_candidates.append((w.get("cited_by_count") or 0, w))
    if oa_candidates:
        oa_candidates.sort(key=lambda t: t[0], reverse=True)
        print(f"\n[7] Open-access full text available for {len(oa_candidates)} of {len(pool)} "
              f"IIT papers — running full-text pipeline on the most-cited one.")
        run_pipeline(oa_candidates[0][1], label="OPEN-ACCESS FULL TEXT", prefix="iit_fulltext")
    print("\nDone.")


def run_pipeline(paper, label="", prefix="out"):
    title = paper.get("title")
    year = paper.get("publication_year")
    cites = paper.get("cited_by_count")
    doi = (paper.get("doi") or "").replace("https://doi.org/", "")
    venue = ((paper.get("primary_location") or {}).get("source") or {}).get("display_name")
    authors = [a["author"]["display_name"] for a in (paper.get("authorships") or [])][:12]
    print(f"\n[2] {label}\n    {title}\n    {venue} ({year}), {cites} citations, doi:{doi}")

    abstract = invert_abstract(paper.get("abstract_inverted_index"))
    print(f"    abstract reconstructed from OpenAlex: {len(abstract)} characters")

    # ---- try to fetch an open-access PDF -----------------------------------
    pdf_url = None
    oa = paper.get("best_oa_location") or {}
    if oa.get("pdf_url"):
        pdf_url = oa["pdf_url"]
    else:
        for loc in paper.get("locations") or []:
            if loc.get("pdf_url"):
                pdf_url = loc["pdf_url"]
                break
    fulltext = ""
    pdf_path = None
    if pdf_url:
        print(f"[3] Open-access PDF found: {pdf_url}")
        data, ctype = _get_bytes(pdf_url)
        if data and (data[:4] == b"%PDF" or "pdf" in ctype.lower()):
            pdf_path = os.path.join(OUT, f"{prefix}_source.pdf")
            with open(pdf_path, "wb") as f:
                f.write(data)
            print(f"    saved {len(data):,} bytes -> {pdf_path}")
            try:
                from pypdf import PdfReader
                reader = PdfReader(pdf_path)
                pages = [(p.extract_text() or "") for p in reader.pages[:60]]
                fulltext = "\n".join(pages)
                print(f"    extracted {len(fulltext):,} characters from {len(reader.pages)} pages")
            except Exception as e:
                print("    [warn] PDF text extraction failed:", e)
        else:
            print("    [warn] PDF endpoint did not return a PDF; falling back to abstract only.")
    else:
        print("[3] No open-access PDF for this paper (paywalled) — using the abstract text.")

    corpus = (abstract + "\n\n" + fulltext).strip() if fulltext else abstract
    if not corpus:
        sys.exit("No text could be obtained.")

    raw_path = os.path.join(OUT, f"{prefix}_raw.txt")
    with open(raw_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"TITLE   : {title}\nAUTHORS : {', '.join(authors)}\n"
                f"VENUE   : {venue} ({year})\nDOI     : {doi}\n"
                f"CITED BY: {cites}\nSOURCE  : OpenAlex (abstract); "
                f"{'open-access PDF' if fulltext else 'abstract only'}\n"
                f"{'='*78}\n\n{abstract}\n")
        if fulltext:
            f.write(f"\n\n{'='*78}\nFULL TEXT (extracted from open-access PDF)\n{'='*78}\n\n{fulltext}\n")
    print(f"[4] Raw text written -> {raw_path}")

    top, ntok, nuniq = top_words(corpus)
    csv_path = os.path.join(OUT, f"{prefix}_word_frequencies.csv")
    with open(csv_path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(["rank", "word", "count", "pct_of_content_words"])
        for i, (word, c) in enumerate(top, 1):
            w.writerow([i, word, c, round(100 * c / max(ntok, 1), 2)])
    md_path = os.path.join(OUT, f"{prefix}_word_frequencies.md")
    with open(md_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"# Top 15 non-stop words — {title[:70]}\n\n"
                f"Corpus: {'abstract + full text' if fulltext else 'abstract only'} | "
                f"{ntok:,} content tokens | {nuniq:,} unique\n\n"
                f"| # | Word | Count | % of content words |\n|---|---|---|---|\n")
        for i, (word, c) in enumerate(top, 1):
            f.write(f"| {i} | {word} | {c} | {100*c/max(ntok,1):.2f}% |\n")
    print(f"[5] Frequency tables written -> {csv_path}\n                               {md_path}")

    meta = {"title": title, "year": year, "venue": venue, "doi": doi,
            "cited_by_count": cites, "authors": authors,
            "openalex_id": paper.get("id"), "pdf_url": pdf_url,
            "pdf_downloaded": bool(pdf_path), "abstract_chars": len(abstract),
            "fulltext_chars": len(fulltext), "content_tokens": ntok,
            "unique_content_tokens": nuniq,
            "top15": [{"word": w, "count": c} for w, c in top]}
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, f"{prefix}_metadata.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(meta, f, indent=2)
    
    print("\n[6] TOP 15 NON-STOP WORDS")
    for i, (w, c) in enumerate(top, 1):
        print(f"    {i:>2}. {w:<18} {c}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | scripts/02_ocr_figure.py | encoding=text | bytes=8834 | sha256=4cde874b9321544eb60b14e42946e6296f46551c66cab51b402d3e6cece183c3
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Part 3B — Download a real, publicly available figure from one of the papers
(Fig. 1 of the Cogitate Consortium 2025 *Nature* paper: the IIT vs GNWT
predictions diagram, hosted open-access in Europe PMC as PMC12137136),
then extract its text/labels with TWO independent OCR engines:

  1. Tesseract 5.5.0 (apt-installed) via pytesseract, with per-word confidence
  2. RapidOCR (ONNX runtime, neural text detector/recogniser)

Outputs (in ../figures and ../data):
  figures/cogitate_fig1.png          the downloaded figure
  figures/cogitate_fig1_upscaled.png 2x upscaled copy fed to the OCR engines
  data/ocr_tesseract.txt             tesseract plain-text output
  data/ocr_tesseract_words.tsv       per-token confidence table
  data/ocr_rapidocr.txt              rapidocr output with confidences
  data/ocr_results.json              structured results + confidence stats
"""

import json
import os
import re
import statistics
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, ".."))
FIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "figures")
DAT = os.path.join(ROOT, "data")
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(DAT, exist_ok=True)

UA = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; IIT-GWT-research-script/1.0)"}
PMCID = "PMC12137136"          # Cogitate Consortium et al., Nature 642:133-142 (2025)
NS = {"xlink": "http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"}


def fetch(url, binary=False, tries=3):
    for i in range(tries):
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
                data = r.read()
            return data if binary else data.decode("utf-8", "ignore")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    [warn] {type(e).__name__} for {url[:70]} — retry {i+1}/{tries}")
    return None


def get_figure_url(pmcid, fig_id="Fig1"):
    """Read the JATS XML from Europe PMC and pull the <graphic> filename for a figure."""
    xml = fetch(f"https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/{pmcid}/fullTextXML")
    if not xml:
        return None, None, None
    root = ET.fromstring(xml)
    for fig in root.iter("fig"):
        if fig.get("id") != fig_id:
            continue
        cap = "".join(fig.find("caption").itertext()) if fig.find("caption") is not None else ""
        cap = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", cap).strip()
        for g in fig.iter("graphic"):
            href = g.get("{http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink}href") or g.get("href")
            if href:
                return href, cap, xml
    return None, None, xml


def candidate_urls(pmcid, href):
    pid = pmcid.replace("PMC", "")
    name = os.path.basename(href)
    return [
        f"https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/{pmcid}/supplementaryFiles/{name}",
        f"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/{pmcid}/bin/{name}",
        f"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/{pmcid}/bin/{name}",
        f"https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/{pmcid}/figures/{name}",
    ]


def main():
    print(f"[1] Resolving figure 'Fig1' in {PMCID} (Cogitate Consortium, Nature 2025)...")
    href, caption, xml = get_figure_url(PMCID)
    if not href:
        # fall back: list all graphics
        root = ET.fromstring(xml or "<x/>")
        hrefs = [g.get("{http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink}href") for g in root.iter("graphic")]
        hrefs = [h for h in hrefs if h]
        print("    Fig1 not found; available graphics:", hrefs[:8])
        href = hrefs[0] if hrefs else None
    print(f"    graphic href : {href}")
    print(f"    caption      : {(caption or '')[:220]}")

    img_bytes = None
    used_url = None
    for u in candidate_urls(PMCID, href):
        print(f"    trying {u}")
        b = fetch(u, binary=True, tries=1)
        if b and len(b) > 5000 and (b[:4] in (b"\x89PNG", b"\xff\xd8\xff") or b[:4] == b"GIF8"):
            img_bytes, used_url = b, u
            break
    if not img_bytes:
        # last resort: the Nature-hosted OA figure
        alt = "https://media.springernature.com/full/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-025-08888-1/MediaObjects/41586_2025_8888_Fig1_HTML.png"
        print("    trying Springer Nature OA CDN...")
        img_bytes = fetch(alt, binary=True, tries=2)
        used_url = alt
    if not img_bytes:
        raise SystemExit("Could not download the figure image.")

    img_path = os.path.join(FIG, "cogitate_fig1.png")
    with open(img_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(img_bytes)
    print(f"[2] Figure downloaded ({len(img_bytes):,} bytes) from {used_url}\n    -> {img_path}")

    img = Image.open(img_path)
    print(f"    format={img.format} mode={img.mode} size={img.size}")
    big = img.convert("RGB")
    big = big.resize((big.width * 2, big.height * 2), Image.LANCZOS)
    up_path = os.path.join(FIG, "cogitate_fig1_upscaled.png")
    big.save(up_path)
    print(f"    upscaled 2x -> {up_path} ({big.size})")

    results = {"source_article": "Cogitate Consortium et al., Nature 642:133-142 (2025)",
               "pmcid": PMCID, "figure": "Fig1", "image_url": used_url,
               "caption": caption, "image_size": list(img.size)}

    # ---------------- 1. Tesseract ----------------
    print("\n[3] Running Tesseract 5.5.0 (pytesseract)...")
    try:
        import pytesseract
        from pytesseract import Output
        txt = pytesseract.image_to_string(big)
        with open(os.path.join(DAT, "ocr_tesseract.txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(txt)
        d = pytesseract.image_to_data(big, output_type=Output.DICT)
        confs, rows = [], []
        for i, tok in enumerate(d["text"]):
            tok = tok.strip()
            if not tok:
                continue
            try:
                c = float(d["conf"][i])
            except ValueError:
                c = -1.0
            if c >= 0:
                confs.append(c)
            rows.append((tok, c, d["left"][i], d["top"][i],
                         d["width"][i], d["height"][i]))
        with open(os.path.join(DAT, "ocr_tesseract_words.tsv"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("token\tconfidence\tleft\ttop\twidth\theight\n")
            for r in rows:
                f.write("\t".join(str(x) for x in r) + "\n")
        words = [r[0] for r in rows if r[1] >= 60]
        results["tesseract"] = {
            "version": str(pytesseract.get_tesseract_version()),
            "tokens": len(rows),
            "mean_confidence": round(statistics.mean(confs), 2) if confs else None,
            "median_confidence": round(statistics.median(confs), 2) if confs else None,
            "tokens_above_60_conf": len(words),
            "text": [t for t in txt.split("\n") if t.strip()][:60],
            "words_above_60": words[:200],
        }
        print(f"    tokens={len(rows)} mean_conf={results['tesseract']['mean_confidence']} "
              f"median_conf={results['tesseract']['median_confidence']}")
    except Exception as e:
        results["tesseract"] = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}
        print("    tesseract failed:", e)

    # ---------------- 2. RapidOCR ----------------
    print("\n[4] Running RapidOCR (ONNX neural OCR)...")
    try:
        from rapidocr_onnxruntime import RapidOCR
        engine = RapidOCR()
        res, _ = engine(up_path)
        lines = []
        confs = []
        with open(os.path.join(DAT, "ocr_rapidocr.txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("text\tconfidence\n")
            for item in res or []:
                box, text, conf = item[0], item[1], float(item[2])
                confs.append(conf)
                lines.append(text)
                f.write(f"{text}\t{conf:.3f}\n")
        results["rapidocr"] = {
            "lines": len(lines),
            "mean_confidence": round(statistics.mean(confs), 3) if confs else None,
            "text": lines[:200],
        }
        print(f"    lines={len(lines)} mean_conf={results['rapidocr']['mean_confidence']}")
    except Exception as e:
        results["rapidocr"] = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}
        print("    rapidocr failed:", e)

    with open(os.path.join(DAT, "ocr_results.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
    print(f"\n[5] Structured results -> {os.path.join(DAT, 'ocr_results.json')}")

    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("TESSERACT TEXT OUTPUT")
    print("=" * 70)
    print(open(os.path.join(DAT, "ocr_tesseract.txt"), encoding="utf-8").read()[:2500])
    if "rapidocr" in results and "text" in results["rapidocr"]:
        print("=" * 70)
        print("RAPIDOCR TEXT OUTPUT")
        print("=" * 70)
        print("\n".join(results["rapidocr"]["text"][:80]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
03_bundle_to_txt.py — bundle every file in this project into ONE plain-text file
(work3.txt) that is easy for a human to read and trivial for a script to split
back into the exact original tree.

Design:
  * Header explains the format and how to extract.
  * A machine-readable JSON MANIFEST lists every file (path, size, sha256, encoding).
  * Each file is wrapped in unique delimiters, with NOTHING else inside the block:

        ====================================================================   <- decorative rule
        <<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | <path> | encoding=<text|base64> | bytes=<n> | sha256=<hex>
        <exact original bytes>
        >>>>>>>>>> FILE_END   | <path>

  * Text files are inlined byte-for-byte (so CRLF and unicode survive).
    Binary files (PDF, PNG) are base64-encoded (76 chars/line).
  * The extractor (extract_work3.py) is embedded as a file block, so the bundle
    is self-contained:   python3 extract_work3.py work3.txt out_dir

Everything is assembled and written in BINARY mode to avoid any newline
translation. Round-trip integrity is verified with SHA-256.
"""

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os

from datetime import datetime, timezone

ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), ".."))
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "work3.txt")

SKIP_NAMES = {"work3.txt", "work3.zip", ".DS_Store"}
SKIP_DIRS = {"__pycache__", ".git", "work3_extracted", "node_modules"}
TEXT_EXT = {".py", ".md", ".txt", ".csv", ".json", ".tsv"}

RULE = b"=" * 100 + b"\n"


def sha256_hex(b: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()


def collect():
    files = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(ROOT):
        dirnames[:] = sorted(d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS)
        for fn in sorted(filenames):
            if fn in SKIP_NAMES or fn.endswith(".pyc"):
                continue
            files.append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, fn), ROOT))
    return sorted(files)


def is_text(rel, data):
    ext = os.path.splitext(rel)[1].lower()
    if b"\x00" in data:
        return False
    if ext in TEXT_EXT:
        try:
            data.decode("utf-8")
            return True
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            return False
    try:
        data.decode("utf-8")
        return True
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return False


def main():
    files = collect()
    manifest, blocks = [], []

    for rel in files:
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, rel), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        text = is_text(rel, data)
        if text:
            enc, body = "text", data
        else:
            enc = "base64"
            b64 = base64.b64encode(data)
            body = b"".join(b64[i:i + 76] + b"\n" for i in range(0, len(b64), 76))
        manifest.append({"path": rel, "encoding": enc, "bytes": len(data),
                         "sha256": sha256_hex(data)})

        # Contract with the extractor: content is followed by EXACTLY one b"\n",
        # and the extractor removes exactly one trailing b"\n". This round-trips
        # both files that end in a newline and files that do not.
        blocks.append(RULE)
        blocks.append(f"<<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | {rel} | encoding={enc} | "
                      f"bytes={len(data)} | sha256={sha256_hex(data)}\n".encode("utf-8"))
        blocks.append(body)
        blocks.append(b"\n")
        blocks.append(f">>>>>>>>>> FILE_END | {rel}\n".encode("utf-8"))
        blocks.append(b"\n")

    total = sum(m["bytes"] for m in manifest)
    n_bin = sum(1 for m in manifest if m["encoding"] == "base64")
    head = []

    head.append(RULE)
    head.append(b"work3.txt - COMPLETE PROJECT BUNDLE (single plain-text archive)\n")
    head.append(RULE)
    head.append(f"Bundle created : {datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')}\n".encode())
    head.append(f"Source tree    : {ROOT}\n".encode())
    head.append(f"Files included : {len(manifest)}  ({len(manifest) - n_bin} text, {n_bin} base64-encoded binary)\n".encode())
    head.append(f"Total size     : {total:,} bytes of original content\n".encode())
    head.append(b"""
WHAT THIS IS
------------
Every file from the IIT-vs-GWT research project, concatenated into one .txt so it can be
read in any text editor, diffed, grepped, or fed to an analysis pipeline. Text files are
inlined byte-for-byte; binary files (the PLOS PDF and the two PNG figures) are base64
encoded so the round trip is lossless.

HOW TO READ IT BY HAND
----------------------
Search (Ctrl-F) for 'FILE_START' to jump between files. Each file sits between:

    <<<<<<<<<< FILE_START | <path> | encoding=<text|base64> | bytes=<n> | sha256=<hex>
    ... exact file content ...
    >>>>>>>>>> FILE_END   | <path>

Suggested reading order:
    1. REPORT.md                          <- the deliverable (Parts 1, 2, 3)
    2. data/iit_fulltext_word_frequencies.md / .csv
    3. data/ocr_tesseract.txt, data/ocr_rapidocr.txt
    4. scripts/01_fetch_iit_paper.py, scripts/02_ocr_figure.py
    5. data/iit_fulltext_raw.txt          <- 133 KB of extracted paper text
    6. everything else (metadata JSON, per-word OCR confidence TSV)

HOW TO SEPARATE THE FILES BACK OUT (lossless, hash-verified)
------------------------------------------------------------
    python3 extract_work3.py work3.txt out_dir     # writes + SHA-256 verifies every file
    python3 extract_work3.py --list work3.txt      # verify only, write nothing

extract_work3.py is INCLUDED as a file block below, so this bundle is self-contained.
""")
    head.append(b"\n" + b"<" * 10 + b" MANIFEST_START (JSON) " + b">" * 10 + b"\n")
    head.append(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2).encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
    head.append(b">" * 10 + b" MANIFEST_END " + b"<" * 10 + b"\n")
    head.append(b"\n" + RULE + b"FILE CONTENTS BEGIN\n" + RULE + b"\n")

    tail = (RULE +
            f"END OF BUNDLE - {len(manifest)} files, {total:,} bytes of original content.\n"
            "Verify any extraction with: python3 extract_work3.py --list work3.txt\n".encode() +
            RULE)

    with open(OUT, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"".join(head) + b"".join(blocks) + tail)

    size = os.path.getsize(OUT)
    print(f"Bundled {len(manifest)} files -> {OUT}")
    print(f"  original bytes : {total:,}")
    print(f"  bundle bytes   : {size:,} ({size/1024/1024:.2f} MiB)")
    for m in manifest:
        print(f"    {m['encoding']:<6} {m['bytes']:>10,}  {m['path']}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
